ucs.title: [LLM] APT32 / OceanLotus DLL side-loading via signed AV/utility binaries staged in user-writable paths
ucs.description: Hunts the OceanLotus (Cobalt Kitty / Canvas Cyclone / BISMUTH) hallmark of dropping a legitimately signed third-party binary (mcoemcpy.exe from McAfee, RasTlsC/RasTlsHost from Symantec, wsc_proxy.exe from Avast, AcroTranscoder.exe from Adobe, SyLauncher.exe) into a non-standard folder so its co-located malicious DLL (McUtil.dll, RasTls.dll, etc.) is loaded via search-order hijacking. The binary names are benign; the give-away is the parent path NOT being the vendor install root.
ucs.splunk: | tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent values(Processes.process_path) as path from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("mcoemcpy.exe","rastlsc.exe","rastlshost.exe","acrotranscoder.exe","wsc_proxy.exe","sylauncher.exe","navlogon.exe","goopdate.exe") AND NOT (Processes.process_path="*\\Program Files\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\Program Files (x86)\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\Windows\\System32\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\*") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where firstTime > relative_time(now(), "-7d") | rename host as dest | table firstTime, lastTime, dest, user, process_name, path, parent, cmdline, count
ucs.kql:
// APT32 / OceanLotus DLL side-load: signed loader binary running OUTSIDE its vendor install path
let OceanLotusLoaders = dynamic(["mcoemcpy.exe","rastlsc.exe","rastlshost.exe","acrotranscoder.exe","wsc_proxy.exe","sylauncher.exe","navlogon.exe","goopdate.exe"]);
let LegitParents = dynamic([@"\Program Files\", @"\Program Files (x86)\", @"\Windows\System32\", @"\Windows\SysWOW64\"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ (OceanLotusLoaders)
| where not (FolderPath has_any (LegitParents))
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (OceanLotusLoaders)
    | where FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\" and FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files"
    | summarize SideLoadedDlls = make_set(FileName, 10), SideLoadedPaths = make_set(FolderPath, 5) by DeviceId, InitiatingProcessId
  ) on DeviceId, $left.ProcessId == $right.InitiatingProcessId
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256, SideLoadedDlls, SideLoadedPaths
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
// Sentinel equivalent — Windows 4688 process create. NewProcessName / CommandLine.
let OceanLotusLoaders = dynamic([@"\mcoemcpy.exe",@"\rastlsc.exe",@"\rastlshost.exe",@"\acrotranscoder.exe",@"\wsc_proxy.exe",@"\sylauncher.exe",@"\navlogon.exe",@"\goopdate.exe"]);
let LegitRoots = dynamic([@"\Program Files\", @"\Program Files (x86)\", @"\Windows\System32\", @"\Windows\SysWOW64\"]);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where tolower(NewProcessName) has_any (OceanLotusLoaders)
| where not (NewProcessName has_any (LegitRoots))
| where TargetUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, TargetUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName, SubjectUserName, TokenElevationType
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\\mcoemcpy.exe OR *\\McOemcpy.exe OR *\\rastlsc.exe OR *\\RasTlsC.exe OR *\\rastlshost.exe OR *\\RasTlsHost.exe OR *\\acrotranscoder.exe OR *\\AcroTranscoder.exe OR *\\wsc_proxy.exe OR *\\Wsc_proxy.exe OR *\\sylauncher.exe OR *\\SyLauncher.exe OR *\\navlogon.exe OR *\\NavLogon.exe OR *\\goopdate.exe OR *\\GoopDate.exe) -@Image:(*\\Program\ Files\\* OR *\\Program\ Files\ \(x86\)\\* OR *\\Windows\\System32\\* OR *\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\*)
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\(mcoemcpy|rastlsc|rastlshost|acrotranscoder|wsc_proxy|sylauncher|navlogon|goopdate)\.exe$/i
| NOT regex("\\\\(Program Files( \\(x86\\))?|Windows\\\\System32|Windows\\\\SysWOW64)\\\\", field=ImageFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName, SHA256HashData], function=count())
| sort(_count, order=desc)
ucs.rationale: APT32 is the public textbook case for this exact technique chain — every major vendor report on OceanLotus (Cybereason 'Cobalt Kitty', ESET, Mandiant FIN-tracker, Microsoft 'BISMUTH') describes the same loader cluster (mcoemcpy + McUtil.dll, RasTlsC + RasTls.dll, wsc_proxy + co-located DLL). ucs.title: [LLM] APT32 / OceanLotus PubPrn.vbs proxy execution of a remote scriptlet (T1216.001)
ucs.description: APT32 was one of the first APT groups observed weaponising the signed Microsoft script PubPrn.vbs to proxy-execute a remote .sct payload via the `script:` moniker — bypassing application allowlisting because the parent is a Microsoft-signed VBS. This UC catches cscript/wscript invoking PubPrn.vbs with either a `script:` URL or any http(s) argument, irrespective of the rest of the command line.
ucs.splunk: | tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("cscript.exe","wscript.exe") AND Processes.process="*pubprn*" AND (Processes.process="*script:*" OR Processes.process="*http://*" OR Processes.process="*https://*") by host Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where firstTime > relative_time(now(), "-30d") | rename host as dest | table firstTime, lastTime, dest, user, process_name, parent, cmdline, count
ucs.kql:
// APT32 PubPrn.vbs script-proxy execution with remote scriptlet — T1216.001
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("cscript.exe","wscript.exe","rundll32.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "pubprn"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("script:", "http://", "https://")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
// Sentinel ASIM port — process_create from any sensor
imProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("cscript.exe","wscript.exe","rundll32.exe")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has "pubprn"
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("script:","http://","https://")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, EventVendor, EventProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: APT32 / OceanLotus PubPrn.vbs Script Proxy Execution
id: a8c3e7c2-5e2f-4b91-9a83-c4d9b7c812f1
status: experimental
description: Detects abuse of the Microsoft-signed PubPrn.vbs to proxy-execute a remote scriptlet via cscript/wscript — a defense-evasion TTP publicly attributed to APT32 (OceanLotus / Cobalt Kitty / BISMUTH).
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1216/001/
  - https://lolbas-project.github.io/lolbas/Scripts/Pubprn/
tags:
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1216.001
  - attack.g0050
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_img:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
  selection_pubprn:
    CommandLine|contains: 'pubprn'
  selection_remote:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'script:'
      - 'http://'
      - 'https://'
  condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate administrative invocation of PubPrn.vbs against a print server (no script: or http(s):// argument)
level: high
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\\cscript.exe OR *\\CScript.exe OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\WScript.exe OR *\\rundll32.exe) @CommandLine:(*pubprn* OR *PubPrn* OR *PUBPRN*) @CommandLine:(*script\:* OR *http\://* OR *https\://*)
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\(wscript|cscript|rundll32)\.exe$/i
| CommandLine=/pubprn/i
| CommandLine=/(script:|https?:\/\/)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
| sort(_count, order=desc)
ucs.rationale: PubPrn.vbs + `script:` moniker is one of the cleanest signature-grade APT32 indicators on record — Casey Smith first published the LOLBin, and OceanLotus operationalised it in the SecureWorks / FireEye-reported 2017-2018 Vietnamese ASEAN-targeted campaigns.
